goulet: 19 participants overall; the extreme-DLMO comparison used 4 morning and 5 evening participants. The protocol covered 7 recording days; the paper does not report a total of valid participant-days.
melidos: Primary near-eye sample: 140 participants, 778 participant-days, and 35,949 valid half-hours.
interpretation: The larger sample supports estimation of individual variation and work/free differences. It does not remove imbalance between chronotype groups and sites.

goulet: Healthy adults aged 19–34, selected by MEQ, with few external constraints on sleep and instructed to keep their preferred sleep schedule.
melidos: Healthy adults who did not work shifts, recruited through several research sites and observed during everyday work and free days.
interpretation: The earlier design reduced schedule variation. MeLiDos captures more everyday variation, but schedules and environments can contribute to group differences.

goulet: MEQ determined morning/evening membership. Laboratory saliva samples measured DLMO, which also defined the intermediate and extreme subsets.
melidos: MSFsc defines the primary quartiles and phase coordinate. MEQ categories provide a sensitivity analysis; DLMO is a published reference guide only.
interpretation: The earlier study measured the biological phase marker needed for its main interpretation. The MEQ sensitivity narrows the difference in group definition, but does not supply measured DLMO.

melidos: Near-eye melanopic EDI, with chest measurements as a placement check; bedside measurements during sleep.
interpretation: Near-eye measurement is a strength for comparing exposure levels. In concurrent MeLiDos recordings, wrist measurements underestimated near-eye melanopic EDI by 30.3%–54.7% across the contexts studied, with larger errors than chest placement (Zauner et al., 2026).

melidos: Multiple locations and dates, with site-specific photoperiod information.
interpretation: MeLiDos can examine whether phase contrasts vary with day length. Uneven chronotype representation across sites limits separation of daylight from geography and related behaviours.

goulet: Hourly averages of log illuminance, group-by-time repeated-measures ANOVA, and comparisons at individual time points.
melidos: Cyclic generalized additive mixed models of half-hour means, with repeated observations, individual curves, day effects, residual correlation, registered contrasts, and held-out prediction.
interpretation: The current models describe smooth timing differences and explicitly represent several sources of dependence.
